output.summary: KEP-5468 introduces a formal approach for testing cluster invariants across an entire end-to-end test run, with ownership, opt-in/out, and flake-demotion rules to limit "tragedy of the commons" flakes in CI. Its status is implemented at stage stable (implementable from 2025-09-30, implemented from 2025-10-14).
output.rationale: SIG Testing received repeated requests to check invariants spanning whole e2e suite runs (e.g., a declarative validation mismatch metric), but suite-wide failures risk flaking in jobs whose authors are not watching. The KEP formalizes the approach with rules: invariants must have documented owners, tests are repeated before merge, and flaking invariants can be demoted with a [Flaky] tag. The maintainer noted it does not affect production binaries, only e2e.test, and was captured so the decision process and maintenance would be recorded.

alternatives.option: Targeting integration tests instead of e2e tests
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal: 'Targeting integration tests. - We are specifically aiming for end to end tests for this purpose.'
Listed as a non-goal in the KEP; the approach is restricted to invariant checks with rules and guardrails.

evidence.quote: we will formalize the approach in this KEP and introduce a principled approach with rules and guardrails
all invariant **MUST** have clearly documented owners, which will be surfaced with the failure results
New invariants will be tested many times before merge, and may be demoted at any time by tagging the associated sentinel test `[Flaky]`
This one is unusual in that it does not impact any binaries you would run in prod (only e2e.test) but we wanted the formal decision making to be captured
